Native FPCA wild-bootstrap truncation selection and inference audit tables

etr_native_wild_source_inference.Rd

One independent native selection algorithm and four source-aligned read-only inference frames from published eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0. The stabilized-volatility selector requires stability_run + 1 consecutive stable width and center transitions and picks the earliest candidate starting such a run for each fixed target. There is no fallback to a largest candidate or automatic calibration.

Usage

etr_select_fpca_wild_bootstrap_truncation(
  scan, width_threshold, center_threshold, stability_run,
  on_failure = "error"
)
etr_fpca_wild_bootstrap_projection_frame(result)
etr_fpca_wild_bootstrap_simultaneous_frame(result)
etr_fpca_wild_bootstrap_family_test_frame(result)
etr_fpca_wild_bootstrap_monte_carlo_diagnostic_frame(result)

Arguments

scan

Explicit R record of an already computed wild-bootstrap truncation scan with candidate components, target curve IDs and candidate-by-target center, width and interval-bound matrices.

width_threshold

Strictly positive width transition threshold, including a finite decimal-text scalar.

center_threshold

Strictly positive center transition threshold, including a finite decimal-text scalar.

stability_run

Nonnegative whole-number r, requiring r+1 successive stable candidate transitions.

on_failure

Whether targets with no qualifying run trigger an error, warning or ignored missing selection.

result

Source-aligned realized projection, simultaneous interval, fixed-family test or Monte Carlo precision diagnostic record.

Details

Published Python eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0 source: wild_selection.py, wild_regression.py, wild_simultaneous.py and wild_testing.py, pinned at c1cd95ad718327550f7e55393ff38582872f7a94.

The selector preserves zero-based chosen candidate index in the result. Target-specific missing selections use NaN, not an unreported fallback. The four audit frames preserve the fixed-target row order, family-adjusted p values, simultaneous interval bounds, and Monte Carlo-sensitive decisions; they do not generate or re-estimate bootstrap quantities. R named-list inputs and R data frame returns are not equivalent to the Python frozen dataclass and pandas source types. This boundary remains a documented unresolved full-contract gap.

Value

Selection returns an explicit R record containing transition matrices, selected source indices, selected values and provenance. Reporting functions return native R data frames. No Python runtime is invoked.
